PullRequest.Title: sessions: start sessions on remote hosts without workspaces, and group artifacts by category
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Follow-up to #348728, with the commits that landed on its branch after it merged. They make a remote agent host that offers no workspace, such as one an extension registers for jobs, work in the Agents window, and let a host group its session artifacts.

## What changes

- **Starting a session on a host that offers no workspace.** The workspace picker offers repositories in a remote environment only when its host offers folders or clones repositories (`canCloneRepository`), since a repository becomes a folder on the host. Choosing an environment with no workspace to offer selects Chat without remembering it as your choice; the picker now keeps that selection itself until a workspace is selected, so the new session gets its draft and model picker instead of staying on Choose Workspace.
- **Session folders that are web addresses.** A session can name its repository by its web address rather than a folder, such as a remote host's session without working directories, and its folder's working directory is then that address. The Agents window now mounts, and looks for customizations in, only session folders a file system provider can read, instead of mounting the address and logging an error for every prompt file location it searched.
- **Artifact categories.** An agent host can give a session artifact a `category`, a name of its choosing such as the kind of decision it waits for. The Artifacts and References pills list such entries in a section of that name, after those of the kinds.

## How to test

1. Register a remote agent host with `vscode.chat.registerRemoteAgentHost` whose host reports no `defaultDirectory` and sessions with a `project` URL but no `workingDirectories`.
2. In the Agents window, start a new session and pick that host as the environment: the workspace shows Chat and the model picker shows the host's models.
3. Open one of its sessions: no workspace folder is mounted and the renderer log has no `Failed to resolve files at location: https://…` errors.
4. Have the host record session artifacts with a `category`: the Artifacts pill lists them under a section with that name.

## Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run oxlint <changed files>`: passed, no warnings
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/sessionArtifacts.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/providers/agentHost/test/browser/agentHostSessionArtifacts.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/chat/sessionArtifacts.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionWorkspacePicker.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/workspace/test/browser/workspaceFolderManagement.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomizationWorkspaceService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts`: 1028 passing
- Manually, in Code OSS against an extension-registered host without workspaces: steps 2 to 4 above.
- Not run: integration or smoke tests.

Scenarios.Scenario: Select a remote environment that offers no folders or repository cloning and prepare its workspace-less draft.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Environment selection checks the available browse actions synchronously, selects Chat, and uses the existing quick-chat draft flow. Model/config readiness depends on configuration resolution; backend creation runs asynchronously after authentication and active-client readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the selected draft's session configuration through the agent connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial resolve for a draft, with a possible second sequential resolve to apply initial configuration; not multiplied by available providers or projects.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This automatic environment-selection branch could leave Choose Workspace selected and create no workspace-less draft. Explicit quick-chat selection already used the same configuration flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Configuration supplies picker options; required initial configuration can also gate backend creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the selected draft's backend session through connection.createSession.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One guarded eager-create task for the new draft, with the existing fallback-on-first-message behavior after failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No automatic draft was created in the newly supported branch. Explicit quick-chat selection already performed this work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs asynchronously; it prepares the backend for the selected session rather than blocking a collection scan.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible providers and their browse actions; existing sessions examined by a host without a default directory; project metadata examined by the clone-capability getter. One selected environment and one intended draft per selection, not one draft per session or project.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Configuration resolution and eager creation use the existing scheduling. Config initialization can make a second sequential resolve when initial values differ. Eager creation is guarded per draft; this change adds no collection-wide launch loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The clone getter reads already-held connection/root state rather than fetching it. Its project parsing is linear in advertised projects. Existing seeded configuration and the eager-create task/backend/subscription guards remain in place. Superseded drafts retain the existing management-layer disposal and cancellation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the changed selection branch through quick-chat creation, initial config resolution, backend creation guards, and superseded-draft ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider/session/project counts and remote initialization latency are not measured. The new remote work is the intended preparation of the explicitly selected session, not redundant fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Additional remote work enables the requested session flow and retains existing scheduling and lifecycle protections.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or switch sessions and mount only readable working-directory folders.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing global Queue serializes workspace updates. Each update awaits worktree trust, the new provider-availability checks, existing folder-trust checks, and any necessary workspace mutation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potentially activate a filesystem-provider extension for a cold, unregistered scheme.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: F in-process availability checks; actual activation is coalesced by scheme/event and extension host, not repeated per folder. Unknown schemes without interested extensions do not cause repeated IPC activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This contribution did not explicitly await provider availability before mounting; subsequent filesystem consumers could already request provider activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold activation must finish before this workspace update mounts folders. Warm registered-provider checks do not wait for activation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing trust resolution and workspace add/remove/update operations, with their downstream configuration and watcher effects.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Trust checks scale with eligible worktrees and readable folders; one batched add/remove/update when the folder set differs, none when it matches. Unsupported web roots are now excluded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All session folders, including unsupported repository web URLs, were considered for mounting. Readable-folder mutation and trust logic already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required workspace mutations finish before the next queued update. Unsupported roots no longer trigger mounting and its downstream work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: F working-directory folders in the selected chat, typically one; U distinct URI schemes among those folders. Repeated session switches enqueue updates as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider checks run in Promise.all within a globally serialized workspace update. Existing trust checks also run in parallel within that update. Extension activation coalesces by scheme/event.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: FileService.canHandleResource activates providers and then checks its scheme map. Registered providers return without waiting for activation joiners. ExtensionHostManager caches activation promises per event, including negative/no-handler outcomes after registry readiness, so F checks do not imply F extension activations or F remote filesystem requests.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected the complete contribution, provider activation implementation, extension activation cache, trust helper, and workspace-editing delegation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold extension-provider activation can be slow, but its duration and occurrence are unknown. No realistic repeated expensive activation was established after accounting for caches; ordinary warm schemes add local checks and a promise barrier.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence regression. The new gate avoids unsupported mounts without introducing per-folder filesystem reads or uncoalesced activation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Discover customizations while opening a project-only remote session or registering a filesystem provider.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The active project root is derived synchronously using hasProvider. Existing customization consumers schedule their refreshes when the derived root changes; prompt discovery resolves configured locations only for applicable roots.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/search configured customization locations and establish file watchers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing work scales with configured locations and readable roots after URI deduplication. No resolve/watch attempts are generated from the filtered unsupported workspace root; user/profile locations remain unaffected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unsupported web roots could be mounted and scanned, leading to repeated failed provider resolutions and error logs across configured locations on discovery/cache invalidation. The PR removes those attempts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery completion affects available customization results, not the synchronous environment capability check.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured prompt locations across observed prompt types, multiplied by mounted readable roots. Unsupported repository web addresses now contribute no mounted root or session-derived customization root.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The new root check starts no async work. Existing discovery iterates configured locations sequentially within a scan, with separate prompt types/consumers using their existing caches and schedulers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: hasProvider is an in-memory scheme lookup. Derived-value equality avoids notifying consumers when unrelated provider registrations leave the root unchanged. Prompt discovery retains per-type cached promises and invalidation events; customization item refresh scheduling remains unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the reduction: traced root derivation, mount filtering, customization observers, prompt-location expansion, filesystem resolution, error logging, and per-type caches.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of configured locations and rediscoveries is workload-dependent. The origin of the URL-as-working-directory behavior could not be resolved with the blame tool, so no provenance-verified regression-fix record was submitted.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The change removes unsupported-root discovery work and adds only a local provider check with reactive invalidation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Read, persist, project, and display categorized session artifacts and references.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing artifact reads parse metadata and map presentation records. Section construction groups the same eligible entries, adding category groups after kind groups. Durable mutations still persist before publication. Dropdown and hover requests keep existing lazy/prefetch behavior.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse and serialize the existing artifact collection, now preserving optional category text.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same collection reads and serializations as before, with one optional bounded output field per categorized record; no per-category serialization pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same artifact collection was parsed and serialized without the category field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Parsing occurs on existing metadata reads; durable mutation serialization remains before publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the merged artifact list through the existing ordered list-visible session-state persistence operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing persistence operation per applied collection mutation, serialized per session; categories introduce no additional persistence calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same merged-list persistence and publication ordering applied without category metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Persistence is awaited before setSessionMeta publishes the mutation, unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch GitHub issue/pull-request hover details through the existing resolver when prefetched or requested.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Initially up to five eligible dropdown entries globally; further visible or interacted entries follow existing behavior. Effective requests deduplicate by target and freshness, with three background resolver jobs at a time; category count does not multiply the cap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same prefetch cap, target cache, in-flight coalescing, and limiter; entries were grouped by kind.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing asynchronous presentation enrichment does not block category grouping.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N recorded entries; K eligible entries after existing chat scope, promotion, alias/resource deduplication, and browser suppression; C distinct categories among those entries, with C at most K. Category normalization is linear in supplied string length; accepted category text is limited to 100 characters.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Grouping remains linear synchronous work. Artifact mutations remain serialized per session. Dropdown initial prefetch is capped at five entries across all sections, not five per category; GitHub background prefetch retains its limiter of three resolver jobs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Category maps are local to section construction, not retained across sessions. Existing artifact-presentation disposal remains unchanged. GitHub details cache by target, coalesce in-flight requests, use freshness checks, and prune unretained targets. Category grouping does not bypass those caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected parser, projection, section construction, mutation persistence, dropdown prefetch, and GitHub resolver caching/concurrency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Artifact/category counts and payload sizes are not profiled. Added category headers and bounded text are proportional to the explicitly requested presentation feature, with no established redundant expensive work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Grouping and retained presentation remain linear in the eligible records, and expensive-boundary counts and concurrency are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all 20 changed files and all diff pages against base 3c2765791fc611b8372133bc6b12d7d4a8d9ac83. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regressions found. Investigated cold provider activation, serialized workspace updates, customization discovery/logging, remote draft initialization, category grouping, persistence, and GitHub prefetch cardinality. Static read-only review; no timings were measured. Unsupported-root discovery work is removed, but blame for the URL-working-directory origin was unavailable; the returned blame for generic folder mounting did not establish the true introducing commit, so no regression-fix provenance record was emitted.
